literal: Yizhou Governor Han Xian held Nandun.
idiomatic: Yizhou governor Han Xian held Nandun.

literal: Xiong again led troops to attack; in a single day he took two of their cities, captured Xian and chief administrator Qiu Yue; Yunbao fled; they seized his wives, concubines, officers, and clerks — two thousand people in all — and sent them all to the capital.
idiomatic: Yao Xiong again led troops to attack; in a single day he took two of their cities, captured Han Xian and chief administrator Qiu Yue; Shi Yunbao fled; they seized his wives, concubines, officers, and clerks — two thousand people in all — and sent them all to the capital.

literal: He was additionally made Grand General of Agile Cavalry.
idiomatic: He was additionally made grand general of agile cavalry.

literal: He still followed Hou Jing in pacifying Luyang and was appointed Governor of Yu Province.
idiomatic: He still followed Hou Jing in pacifying Luyang and was appointed governor of Yu Province.

literal: Though Xiong was a military man, his nature was generous and mild; in governing the people he was quite trustworthy; in administration he cast off petty detail and grasped only the great outline.
idiomatic: Though Yao Xiong was a military man, his nature was generous and mild; in governing the people he was quite trustworthy; in administration he cast off petty detail and grasped only the great outline.

literal: He nurtured soldiers and commoners alike and gained their useful strength.
idiomatic: He nurtured soldiers and commoners alike and gained their useful strength.

literal: At the frontier for ten years he repeatedly achieved merit; the people of Yu still cherish his memory to this day.
idiomatic: At the frontier for ten years he repeatedly achieved merit; the people of Yu still cherish his memory to this day.

literal: He also loved talented men and gave generously; guests coming and going received lavish courtesy and gifts — for this too he won renown.
idiomatic: He also loved talented men and gave generously; guests coming and going received lavish courtesy and gifts — for this too he won renown.

literal: In the third year of Xinghe he was recalled to the capital; soon he was put in command of a hundred thousand soldiers from the ten provinces of Si, Ji, Ying, Ding, Qi, Qing, Jiao, Yan, Yin, and Cang, touring the southwest and assigning garrisons at strategic passes.
idiomatic: In the third year of Xinghe he was recalled to the capital; soon he was put in command of a hundred thousand soldiers from the ten provinces of Si, Ji, Ying, Ding, Qi, Qing, Jiao, Yan, Yin, and Cang, touring the southwest and assigning garrisons at strategic passes.

literal: In the fourth year he died at Ye; he was forty-four.
idiomatic: In the fourth year he died at Ye. He was forty-four.

literal: Posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff, command over military affairs in the three provinces of Qing, Xu, and Jiao, Grand General, Minister over the Masses, Governor of Xu Province; posthumous title Wugong.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff, command over military affairs in the three provinces of Qing, Xu, and Jiao, grand general, minister over the masses, and governor of Xu Province; posthumous title Wugong.

literal: His son Shisi succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Shisi succeeded.

literal: Xiong's younger brother Fen, styled Yanju.
idiomatic: Yao Xiong's younger brother Fen, styled Yanju.

literal: On entering office he was made General Who Proclaims Might and Gentleman within the Gates; transferred to General of the Central Guard and Grand Master for the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; granted the title Viscount of Anyi County.
idiomatic: On entering office he was made general who proclaims might and gentleman within the gates; transferred to general of the central guard and grand master for the golden seal and purple ribbon; granted the title viscount of Anyi County.

literal: Following Gao Huan in pacifying Ye and defeating Erzhu Zhao and others, his rank was advanced to Baron.
idiomatic: Following Gao Huan in pacifying Ye and defeating Erzhu Zhao and others, his rank was advanced to baron.

literal: Sent out as Governor of Southern Fen Province; the Hu and barbarian peoples feared and respected him.
idiomatic: Sent out as governor of Southern Fen Province; the Hu and barbarian peoples feared and respected him.

literal: Western Wei mobile-office commissioner Xue Chongli raised troops to attack Fen; they gave battle and inflicted a great defeat; Chongli and his brothers begged to surrender and were sent to the chief minister's headquarters.
idiomatic: Western Wei mobile-office commissioner Xue Chongli raised troops to attack Fen; they gave battle and inflicted a great defeat; Chongli and his brothers begged to surrender and were sent to the chief minister's headquarters.

literal: Fen was transferred to Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Governor of Ying Province, then died.
idiomatic: Fen was transferred to grand general of agile cavalry, left grand master for splendid happiness, and governor of Ying Province, then died.

literal: Posthumously granted command over military affairs in the three provinces of Yan, Yu, and Liang, Minister of Works, and Governor of Yan Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted command over military affairs in the three provinces of Yan, Yu, and Liang, minister of works, and governor of Yan Province.

literal: Xiong's paternal cousin Jie, styled Shou.
idiomatic: Yao Xiong's paternal cousin Jie, styled Shou.

literal: His nature was reckless and impulsive; he loved wine and possessed considerable martial skill.
idiomatic: His nature was reckless and impulsive; he loved wine and possessed considerable martial skill.

literal: He successively served as Gentleman within the Gates and Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard.
idiomatic: He successively served as gentleman within the gates and supervisor of the Feathered Forest guard.

literal: Following Gao Huan in defeating Hedouling Bufan he had merit and was made General Who Pacifies the East.
idiomatic: Following Gao Huan in defeating Hedouling Bufan he had merit and was made general who pacifies the east.

literal: Enfeoffed Baron of Lecheng County with a fief of a hundred households.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed baron of Lecheng County with a fief of a hundred households.

literal: Sent out as Governor of Cang Province.
idiomatic: Sent out as governor of Cang Province.

literal: When the righteous host was raised, he returned to Gao Huan.
idiomatic: When the righteous host was raised, he returned to Gao Huan.

literal: Following in the pacification of Ye and the defeat of Erzhu Zhao, his rank was advanced to Marquis.
idiomatic: Following in the pacification of Ye and the defeat of Erzhu Zhao, his rank was advanced to marquis.

literal: Later as Area Commander he led troops following Fan Zihu in campaigning against Yuan Shu at Qiao City and pacified him.
idiomatic: Later as area commander he led troops following Fan Zihu in campaigning against Yuan Shu at Qiao City and pacified him.

literal: He was still appointed to Southern Yan Province; he accepted many bribes, yet his nature was resolute and decisive, and officials and commoners feared him.
idiomatic: He was still appointed to Southern Yan Province; he accepted many bribes, yet his nature was resolute and decisive, and officials and commoners feared him.

literal: Soon he was additionally put in charge of Yan Province affairs.
idiomatic: Soon he was additionally put in charge of Yan Province affairs.

literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang he was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commissioner with Protocol Equal to Three Imperators; his rank was advanced to Duke.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanxiang he was appointed grand general of chariots and cavalry and commissioner with protocol equal to three imperators; his rank was advanced to duke.

literal: Sent out as Grand Commander of Mocheng Garrison; transferred to Governor of An Province; died in office.
idiomatic: Sent out as grand commander of Mocheng garrison; transferred to governor of An Province; died in office.

literal: Posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff, command over military affairs in Cang and Ying provinces, Right Vice Director in the Masters of Writing, Governor of Cang Province; posthumous title left blank.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff, command over military affairs in Cang and Ying provinces, right vice director in the masters of writing, and governor of Cang Province; posthumous title left blank.

literal: Song Xian, styled Zhonghua, was a native of Xiaogu in Dunhuang.
idiomatic: Song Xian, styled Zhonghua, was a native of Xiaogu in Dunhuang.

literal: His nature was bold and resolute, with practical ability.
idiomatic: His nature was bold and resolute, with practical ability.

literal: At first he served Erzhu Rong as army commander and was promoted to long-term-flow adjutant.
idiomatic: At first he served Erzhu Rong as army commander and was promoted to long-term-flow adjutant.

literal: During Yongan he was made front-army commander and Governor of Xiangyuan; transferred to record-keeping adjutant in Rong's headquarters.
idiomatic: During Yongan he was made front-army commander and governor of Xiangyuan; transferred to record-keeping adjutant in Rong's headquarters.

literal: Following in the pacification of Yuan Hao, he was additionally made General Who Pacifies the East.
idiomatic: Following in the pacification of Yuan Hao, he was additionally made general who pacifies the east.

literal: When Rong died and Shilong and others marched on Luoyang, Xian was again appointed Governor of Xiangyuan.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died and Erzhu Shilong and others marched on Luoyang, Song Xian was again appointed governor of Xiangyuan.

literal: At the beginning of Putai he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, General Who Campaigns North, and Governor of Jin Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Putai he was transferred to bearer of the staff, general who campaigns north, and governor of Jin Province.

literal: Later he returned to Gao Huan and was made Right Vice Director in the Mobile Office.
idiomatic: Later he returned to Gao Huan and was made right vice director in the mobile office.

literal: Fan Zihu held Yan Province in rebellion; former Western Yan Province Governor Yi Yuan and Qiao Commandery Governor Xin Jingwei garrisoned Wuliang in response to Zihu.
idiomatic: Fan Zihu held Yan Province in rebellion; former Western Yan Province governor Yi Yuan and Qiao Commandery governor Xin Jingwei garrisoned Wuliang in response to Zihu.

literal: Gao Huan put Xian in charge of Western Yan Province affairs; he led troops, defeated them, beheaded Yuan, and Jingwei fled.
idiomatic: Gao Huan put Song Xian in charge of Western Yan Province affairs; he led troops, defeated them, beheaded Yi Yuan, and Xin Jingwei fled.

literal: He was appointed Governor of Western Yan Province.
idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Western Yan Province.

literal: At that time Liang Province Governor Lu Yongji held the province and rebelled; Western Wei sent Prince Yuan Yue of Boling and Prince Yuan Jingshen of Zhao Commandery with troops to welcome him.
idiomatic: At that time Liang Province governor Lu Yongji held the province and rebelled; Western Wei sent Prince Yuan Yue of Boling and Prince Yuan Jingshen of Zhao Commandery with troops to welcome him.

literal: Xian mustered the province's troops and cavalry, intercepted and defeated them, beheaded Yue and the others, then joined Left Guard General Hulu Ping at Daliang.
idiomatic: Song Xian mustered the province's troops and cavalry, intercepted and defeated them, beheaded Yuan Yue and the others, then joined left guard general Hulu Ping at Daliang.

literal: He was appointed Commissioner with Protocol Equal to Three Imperators.
idiomatic: He was appointed commissioner with protocol equal to three imperators.

literal: In the province he accepted many bribes, yet he was bold, resolute, and capable; in inspecting and controlling those around him, he could always win their wholehearted effort.
idiomatic: In the province he accepted many bribes, yet he was bold, resolute, and capable; in inspecting and controlling those around him, he could always win their wholehearted effort.

literal: At the battle of Heyin he plunged deep to meet the enemy and perished in the battle line.
idiomatic: At the battle of Heyin he plunged deep to meet the enemy and perished in the battle line.

literal: Posthumously granted Minister of Works.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted minister of works.

literal: Xian's second cousin Hui from youth studied diligently and read widely; he loved composing and annotating. In Wei times Zhang Mian's Book of Jin had not entered the realm; Hui, following the model of Pei Songzhi's commentary on the Records of the Three Kingdoms, annotated Wang Yin's works and the Book of the Restoration.
idiomatic: Song Xian's second cousin Hui from youth studied diligently and read widely; he loved composing and annotating. In Wei times Zhang Mian's Book of Jin had not entered the realm; Hui, following the model of Pei Songzhi's commentary on the Records of the Three Kingdoms, annotated Wang Yin's works and the Book of the Restoration.

literal: He also composed the Ten Scrolls of Biographies of Many Scholars of the Central Court and the Fifty Chapters of Genealogical Records of Clans.
idiomatic: He also composed the Ten Scrolls of Biographies of Many Scholars of the Central Court and the Fifty Chapters of Genealogical Records of Clans.

literal: Because various households' chronologies differed and contained many errors, he collated and corrected discrepancies and composed a Chronological Record — it was unfinished when in the fifth year of Heqing both works were lost in a flood.
idiomatic: Because various households' chronologies differed and contained many errors, he collated and corrected discrepancies and composed a Chronological Record — it was unfinished when in the fifth year of Heqing both works were lost in a flood.

literal: Though Hui was broadly learned with a strong memory, his native disposition was absent-minded; in his later years he also suffered a wind ailment and his speech grew slow.
idiomatic: Though Hui was broadly learned with a strong memory, his native disposition was absent-minded; in his later years he also suffered a wind ailment and his speech grew slow.

literal: When the books he had composed were lost, he beat his breast and wept bitterly, saying: "This is truly Heaven's deathblow to me!
idiomatic: When the books he had composed were lost, he beat his breast and wept bitterly, saying: "This is truly Heaven's deathblow to me!

literal: " In the Tiantong era he died.
idiomatic: " In the Tiantong era he died.

literal: Wang Ze, styled Yuangui, claimed to be from Taiyuan.
idiomatic: Wang Ze, styled Yuangui, claimed to be from Taiyuan.

literal: From youth he was daring and resolute, with martial skill.
idiomatic: From youth he was daring and resolute, with martial skill.

literal: At first he followed his uncle, Wei interior secretary of Guangping Laisheng, on campaigns; each time he won military merit.
idiomatic: At first he followed his uncle, Wei interior secretary of Guangping Laisheng, on campaigns; each time he won military merit.

literal: Laisheng came to be known to the court, and Ze had considerable influence through him.
idiomatic: Laisheng came to be known to the court, and Wang Ze had considerable influence through him.

literal: At first for military merit he was made Gentleman within the Gates and granted the title Viscount of Baishui.
idiomatic: At first for military merit he was made gentleman within the gates and granted the title viscount of Baishui.

literal: Later following Yuan Tianmu in campaigning against Xing Gao, he led light cavalry deep in and was captured by Gao.
idiomatic: Later following Yuan Tianmu in campaigning against Xing Gao, he led light cavalry deep in and was captured by Gao.

literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Ze and Laisheng both surrendered to Hao; Hao suspected Laisheng and thereupon killed him.
idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Wang Ze and Laisheng both surrendered to Hao; Hao suspected Laisheng and thereupon killed him.

literal: Ze fled to Guangzhou Governor Zheng Xianhu, and together they resisted Hao; when Hao was defeated, Ze was promoted to General Who Subdues Captives and sent out as Area Commander defending the walls of Eastern Xu Province.
idiomatic: Wang Ze fled to Guangzhou governor Zheng Xianhu, and together they resisted Hao; when Hao was defeated, Ze was promoted to general who subdues captives and sent out as area commander defending the walls of Eastern Xu Province.

literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Eastern Xu Province Governor Hus Chun was one of his faction and inwardly feared; at that time Liang set up Prince Yue of Runan of Wei as ruler of Wei, supplied him with troops and horses, and escorted him to the border; Chun thereupon turned the city and surrendered to Yue; Ze together with Lanling Governor Li Yi struck their flank army and defeated it.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died, Eastern Xu Province governor Hus Chun was one of his faction and inwardly feared; at that time Liang set up Prince Yue of Runan of Wei as ruler of Wei, supplied him with troops and horses, and escorted him to the border; Chun thereupon turned the city and surrendered to Yue; Wang Ze together with Lanling governor Li Yi struck their flank army and defeated it.

literal: Wei thereupon put Ze in charge of Northern Xu Province affairs; later he came under Erzhu Zhongyuan; when Zhongyuan was defeated, he at last returned to Gao Huan.
idiomatic: Wei thereupon put Wang Ze in charge of Northern Xu Province affairs; later he came under Erzhu Zhongyuan; when Zhongyuan was defeated, he at last returned to Gao Huan.

literal: He was still additionally made General Who Campaigns South and Grand Master for the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
idiomatic: He was still additionally made general who campaigns south and grand master for the golden seal and purple ribbon.

literal: At first he followed Jing Province Governor Heba Sheng; later he followed mobile-office commissioner Hou Jing, campaigning back and forth with repeated merit.
idiomatic: At first he followed Jing Province governor Heba Sheng; later he followed mobile-office commissioner Hou Jing, campaigning back and forth with repeated merit.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping he administered Jing Province affairs, commanding military affairs in the six provinces of the three Jing, two Xiang, and Southern Yong, and serving as Governor of Jing Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he administered Jing Province affairs, commanding military affairs in the six provinces of the three Jing, two Xiang, and Southern Yong, and serving as governor of Jing Province.

literal: Ze had martial prestige; frontier peoples feared and submitted to him.
idiomatic: Wang Ze had martial prestige; frontier peoples feared and submitted to him.

literal: At the battle of Weiqu, Ze was pressed hard by Western Wei forces and abandoned the city to flee to Liang.
idiomatic: At the battle of Weiqu, Wang Ze was pressed hard by Western Wei forces and abandoned the city to flee to Liang.

literal: Liang soon sent him back; Gao Huan was angry but did not punish him.
idiomatic: Liang soon sent him back; Gao Huan was angry but did not punish him.

literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang he was appointed Governor of Luo Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanxiang he was appointed governor of Luo Province.

literal: Ze's nature was greedy; in the province he accepted unlawful bribes; he destroyed the old capital's statues to cast coin — at the time the age called them Heyang coin, and all came from his household.
idiomatic: Wang Ze's nature was greedy; in the province he accepted unlawful bribes; he destroyed the old capital's statues to cast coin — at the time the age called them Heyang coin, and all came from his household.

literal: During Wuding he again followed Hou Jing on the western campaign.
idiomatic: During Wuding he again followed Hou Jing on the western campaign.

literal: When Jing rebelled at Yingchuan, Ze was then garrisoning the Biya garrison; Gao Cheng, because Ze had martial ability, summoned him to be Governor of Xu Province.
idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled at Yingchuan, Wang Ze was then garrisoning the Biya garrison; Gao Cheng, because Ze had martial ability, summoned him to be governor of Xu Province.

literal: Once Jing had submitted to the south, Liang sent the Marquis of Zhenyang Xiao Ming with a great host toward Xu Province as coordinated support, damming the Qing River to flood the provincial city.
idiomatic: Once Hou Jing had submitted to the south, Liang sent the marquis of Zhenyang Xiao Ming with a great host toward Xu Province as coordinated support, damming the Qing River to flood the provincial city.

literal: Ze held firm for a long time, but his bribe-taking was outrageous; he was chained and sent to Jinyang; Gao Cheng pardoned his crime.
idiomatic: Wang Ze held firm for a long time, but his bribe-taking was outrageous; he was chained and sent to Jinyang; Gao Cheng pardoned his crime.

literal: In spring of the seventh year of Wuding he died; he was forty-eight.
idiomatic: In spring of the seventh year of Wuding he died. He was forty-eight.

literal: Posthumously granted command over military affairs in Qing and Qi provinces, Minister of Works, Governor of Qing Province; posthumous title Lieyi.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted command over military affairs in Qing and Qi provinces, minister of works, and governor of Qing Province; posthumous title Lieyi.

literal: Wang Jingbao
idiomatic: Wang Jingbao

literal: Ze's younger brother Jingbao from youth rose through prominent posts.
idiomatic: Wang Ze's younger brother Jingbao from youth rose through prominent posts.

literal: Later as Governor of Eastern Guang Province he joined Xiao Gui and others in attacking Jianye, failed to take it, and perished there.
idiomatic: Later as governor of Eastern Guang Province he joined Xiao Gui and others in attacking Jianye, failed to take it, and perished there.

literal: Murong Shaozong
idiomatic: Murong Shaozong

literal: Murong Shaozong was a descendant of Prince Ke of Taiyuan, fourth son of Murong Huang; his great-grandfather Teng submitted to Wei and thereafter settled in Dai.
idiomatic: Murong Shaozong was a descendant of Prince Ke of Taiyuan, fourth son of Murong Huang; his great-grandfather Teng submitted to Wei and thereafter settled in Dai.

literal: His grandfather Du was Governor of Qi Province.
idiomatic: His grandfather Du was governor of Qi Province.

literal: His father Yuan was Governor of Heng Province.
idiomatic: His father Yuan was governor of Heng Province.

literal: Shaozong's bearing was broad and resolute; he spoke little; he was deep and steady, with courage and design.
idiomatic: Shaozong's bearing was broad and resolute; he spoke little; he was deep and steady, with courage and design.

literal: Erzhu Rong was his mother's sister's son.
idiomatic: Erzhu Rong was his mother's sister's son.

literal: When the northern frontier was in turmoil, Shaozong brought his household to Jinyang to join Rong; Rong treated him with deep favor.
idiomatic: When the northern frontier was in turmoil, Shaozong brought his household to Jinyang to join Rong; Rong treated him with deep favor.

literal: When Rong raised troops and entered Luoyang, he privately told Shaozong: "The gentry of Luoyang are numerous; pride and extravagance have become custom; if they are not cut down, I fear they will be hard to control.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong raised troops and entered Luoyang, he privately told Shaozong: "The gentry of Luoyang are numerous; pride and extravagance have become custom; if they are not cut down, I fear they will be hard to control.

literal: I wish to take the occasion when all officials come out to welcome me and put them all to the sword — what do you say, is that feasible?
idiomatic: I wish to take the occasion when all officials come out to welcome me and put them all to the sword — what do you say, is that feasible?

literal: " Shaozong replied: "The Empress Dowager holds court, licentious and cruel without the Way; the realm burns with indignation — all have cast her off.
idiomatic: " Shaozong replied: "The empress dowager holds court, licentious and cruel without the Way; the realm burns with indignation — all have cast her off.

literal: Your Lordship now holds divine troops in hand and keeps loyalty and righteousness in heart; suddenly to wish to slaughter many scholars — I think that is no long-term plan; I deeply hope you will think thrice.
idiomatic: Your Lordship now holds divine troops in hand and keeps loyalty and righteousness in heart; suddenly to wish to slaughter many scholars — I think that is no long-term plan; I deeply hope you will think thrice.

literal: " Rong did not heed him.
idiomatic: " Rong did not heed him.

literal: Later for military merit he was enfeoffed Viscount of Suolu County.
idiomatic: Later for military merit he was enfeoffed viscount of Suolu County.

literal: Soon his rank was advanced to Marquis.
idiomatic: Soon his rank was advanced to marquis.

literal: Following Gao Huan in defeating Yang Kan, and with Yuan Tianmu in pacifying Xing Gao, he rose in succession to Governor of Bing Province.
idiomatic: Following Gao Huan in defeating Yang Kan, and with Yuan Tianmu in pacifying Xing Gao, he rose in succession to governor of Bing Province.

literal: Hedouling Bufan pressed on Jinyang; Erzhu Zhao attacked him but was repeatedly broken by Bufan; Zhao wished to summon Gao Huan from Jin Province to join in plotting against Bufan.
idiomatic: Hedouling Bufan pressed on Jinyang; Erzhu Zhao attacked him but was repeatedly broken by Bufan; Zhao wished to summon Gao Huan from Jin Province to join in plotting against Bufan.

literal: Shaozong remonstrated, saying: "Today the realm is in turmoil; men harbor covetous designs.
idiomatic: Shaozong remonstrated, saying: "Today the realm is in turmoil; men harbor covetous designs.
